summary: G. B. Beaman (1870–1942) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Cincinnati (~1889–1893), the University of Jena (1893), and the University of Leipzig (Ph.D. 1894–1895), where he studied under Ernst Windisch.

G. B. Palsule (1920–2007) was an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute as a dictionary sub-editor (attested 1957) and at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1987).
Indologist G. Herberich completed a Ph.D. at the University of Würzburg by 1893, studying under Julius Jolly.
G. K. Jenkins (1918–2005) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Bloxham School and held a post at the British Museum from 1947 to 1978.

G. P. Malalasekera (1899–1973) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of London and SOAS under Caroline Rhys Davids and William Stede, he held posts at University College, Colombo, and the University of Ceylon.

G. Rita Dudley-Grant worked in Buddhist studies and health. She studied at NHS Grampian and Robert Gordon University, later serving at Virgin Islands Behavioral Sciences (attested 2003) and as an advanced practitioner physiotherapist at NHS Grampian (2004).

G. S. Sahay specializes in Indology and philosophy. After working at Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center (attested 2005) and studying at the University of Nebraska Medical Center, Sahay held posts at MIT and Oregon State University.
G. Srinivasa Murti was a scholar in Indology. He served as the Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre, with his tenure attested in 1938–1949 and in 1971.

G. Thomas Tanselle (born 1934) studied at Yale. He held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1960–1978) and Columbia University (~1978–2006), and served as vice president of the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation (1978–2006).
G. V. Aston specializes in philosophy and religious studies. Aston earned a Ph.D. in philosophy at the University of Canterbury (1986–2004), studying under Paul Harrison.

G. V. Srinivasa Rao was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He served as Senior Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India until 1945 and retired from the office of the Government Epigraphist for India.

id: P:Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso
summary: Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Gabriel Engelsmann (1858–1924) was an Indology scholar who earned a Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (~1881–1885), where he studied under Georg Bühler.
Gabriel Jouveau-Dubreuil (1885–1945) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He taught at Lycée Français de Pondichéry (1909) and completed a Ph.D. at the University of Paris (~1910–1914).

Gadjin Nagao (1907–2005) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Kyoto University under Ryotai Hatani and Susumu Yamaguchi, he later held the Chair of Buddhist Studies at Kyoto University (1935–1971).
Gail Hinich Sutherland works in religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Chicago under Carol Bolon, Wendy Doniger, and Virendra Singh.

Galuh Nur Fattah works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. After earning an M.Phil. from Gadjah Mada University (2021–2023), Fattah served as Assistant Professor there (2024–2025) and became a lecturer at Sekolah Tinggi Agama Buddha Negeri Raden Wijaya (2025).

Gananath Obeyesekere (1930–2025) studied at the University of Ceylon and University of Washington in religious and Buddhist studies. He taught at the University of Ceylon, UC San Diego, and was an anthropology professor at Princeton University (1980–2000).

Ganesh Prasad (1876–1935) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology educated at Allahabad and Calcutta. He headed a department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1905) and held professorships at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Calcutta.

Ganganatha Jha (1872–1941) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Calcutta and Allahabad. He served as professor at Muir Central College, principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and vice chancellor of the University of Allahabad (1923–1932).
